perk.progressive_adventure.birds_nest.de: Chopping logs sometimes finds a bird's nest with feathers, eggs or string, and once in a while an emerald.

perk.progressive_adventure.relic_sense.d: While holding a brush or shovel, sparkles point towards the nearest suspicious sand or gravel within 16 blocks. Brush it to find treasure!
perk.progressive_adventure.excavator.des: Shovels dig a 3×3 square at once. Sneak to dig a single block.

perk.progressive_adventure.quick_study.d: Each kill counts double towards mob familiarity.
perk.progressive_adventure.careful_sweep: Your sword sweep no longer hurts pets, villagers or golems standing near the mob you hit.
When your sword sweeps, the other mobs nearby take a quarter of your hit extra.
When your sword sweeps, the other mobs nearby take half of your hit extra.
perk.progressive_adventure.whirlwind.des: Sneak while you sweep with a sword: you spin and hit every hostile mob around you, not only the ones next to your target.
perk.progressive_adventure.disarm.descri: 15% chance that a sword hit knocks the weapon out of a mob's hand. A skeleton without its bow has to come close!
perk.progressive_adventure.heavy_swing.d: A fully charged axe hit knocks the mob far back and slows it for 2 seconds.
perk.progressive_adventure.sunder.descri: A fully charged axe hit cracks the mob's armor: it has half its armor for 5 seconds. Great against Tough mobs in heavy armor.
Holding a mace in the air, press sneak to slam straight down. You take no fall damage and push the mobs around you away.
perk.progressive_adventure.shockwave.des: Your mace smash and Ground Pound also hurt the hostile mobs around you for 30% of a mace hit. The higher you fall, the harder it hits.
perk.progressive_adventure.shockwave_2.d: Shockwave hurts the mobs around you for 65% of a mace hit.
perk.progressive_adventure.shockwave_3.d: Shockwave hurts the mobs around you for the full damage of a mace hit.
perk.progressive_adventure.running_charg: Your spear charge on foot hits as if you were much faster: more damage, and it can knock riders off their mounts.
perk.progressive_adventure.pinning_jab.d: Every hostile mob your spear jab hits is slowed for a moment.
perk.progressive_adventure.hearty_kill_1: Defeating a hostile mob heals half a heart.
perk.progressive_adventure.hearty_kill_2: Defeating a hostile mob heals one heart.
perk.progressive_adventure.hearty_kill_3: Defeating a hostile mob heals one and a half hearts.
perk.progressive_adventure.steady_healin: Healing your hearts makes you 25% less hungry.
Healing your hearts makes you 50% less hungry.
perk.progressive_adventure.quick_healing: With a full stomach you heal half a heart every 3 seconds instead of every 4.
With a full stomach you heal half a heart every 2 seconds.
perk.progressive_adventure.deep_reserves: You keep healing until your hunger bar drops below 4 food icons, instead of 9.
perk.progressive_adventure.second_wind.d: Dropping below 3 hearts gives you a burst of regeneration. Recharges after 2 minutes.
perk.progressive_adventure.keepsake_1.de: When you die, you keep the armor you are wearing.
perk.progressive_adventure.keepsake_2.de: When you die, you also keep your hotbar and the item in your other hand.
perk.progressive_adventure.keepsake_3.de: When you die, you lose nothing: you keep all your items and your XP.
perk.progressive_adventure.way_back.desc: After you die, a red trail shows the way back to the spot for 5 minutes.
perk.progressive_adventure.faithful_frie: When your pet would die, it faints and runs back to you instead, if you are in the same dimension. It sits down to rest until you tell it to stand up.
message.progressive_adventure.way_back: You died at %s %s %s. Follow the red trail! It lasts %s minutes.
message.progressive_adventure.way_back_o: You died at %s %s %s in another dimension. The red trail shows when you go there. It lasts %s minutes.
message.progressive_adventure.faithful_f: %s fainted and ran back to you. It is resting now.
perk.progressive_adventure.thrifty_quive: 10% chance a shot doesn't use up an arrow. That arrow can't be picked up again.
20% chance a shot doesn't use up an arrow. That arrow can't be picked up again.
30% chance a shot doesn't use up an arrow. That arrow can't be picked up again.
perk.progressive_adventure.fire_arrows.d: 15% chance your arrow is on fire and sets the mob it hits on fire.
15% chance your arrow is icy and slows the mob it hits for 3 seconds.
perk.progressive_adventure.piercing_shot: Your arrows fly through the first mob they hit and can hit one more.
perk.progressive_adventure.steady_aim.de: Your arrows curve a little toward hostile mobs in front of them. Never toward animals, villagers or pets.
perk.progressive_adventure.ricochet.desc: When your arrow hits a mob, it bounces on to one more hostile mob nearby.
perk.progressive_adventure.loyal_trident: Tridents you throw always come back to you, like with Loyalty.
perk.progressive_adventure.keen_eye.desc: A bell rings when a fish bites, and you get more time to reel it in.
perk.progressive_adventure.lucky.descrip: Catch more treasure and less junk when fishing (like Luck of the Sea II).
25% chance to catch two fish at once.
perk.progressive_adventure.treasure_hunt: Catch treasure anywhere, even in a small pond. Normally treasure needs big open water.
perk.progressive_adventure.bonus_heart_1: +1 heart, on top of the hearts from milestones.
Immune to the Hunger effect from rotten flesh, raw chicken and husks.
Fall 3 more blocks before taking damage.
perk.progressive_adventure.spring_step.d: Jump higher, high enough to hop over fences.
perk.progressive_adventure.step_up.descr: Walk up full blocks without jumping.
perk.progressive_adventure.sure_feet.des: Soul sand and honey blocks no longer slow you down.
perk.progressive_adventure.shadow_step_1: While you sneak, mobs only notice you when you are much closer.
perk.progressive_adventure.shadow_step_2: Sneak more than 8 blocks away from a mob that is chasing you and it loses track of you. Hitting it makes it find you again.
perk.progressive_adventure.mantle.descri: Jump at a wall up to 2 blocks high while walking forward and you pull yourself up onto it.
perk.progressive_adventure.double_jump.d: Press jump again in the air to jump once more. Doesn't work while wearing an elytra.
perk.progressive_adventure.diver.descrip: Mine underwater as fast as on land.
perk.progressive_adventure.shield_bash.d: Attack while your shield is up to push the mobs in front of you away.
perk.progressive_adventure.parry.descrip: Raise your shield just before a mob hits you: the hit goes back to the attacker (up to 4 hearts) and knocks it away.
perk.progressive_adventure.deflect.descr: Raise your shield just before an arrow hits you: it flies straight back at the one who shot it.

achievement.progressive_adventure.tip.mi: You need all 55 biomes of the Overworld. This page shows exactly which ones you're still missing.
Cave biomes count too: lush caves, dripstone caves and the deep dark. Ocean types count separately as well.
Boats are fast for oceans. A cartographer's maps help, and so do waypoints. Rare ones like Mushroom Fields and Badlands take a long trip.
You need exactly Piercing IV. Throw a splash Potion of Poison at 5 different kinds of mobs in a pen: it brings them to almost no health. Then shoot straight down through them from above.
Sculk sensors are blue blocks with little feelers, found in the deep dark. Hold the sneak key and walk near one.
You have to be within 8 blocks of it, and sneaking the whole time. A sensor is much safer than a warden, so stay away from those!
Hit a Breeze's wind charge at the right moment and it flies back. A deflected charge only does a tiny bit of damage, so the Breeze must be almost dead.
The trick is Poison: it brings a Breeze down to half a heart without killing it. Trial chamber dispensers sometimes shoot it, or throw your own splash potion.
When the poison ends, stop hitting the Breeze and just click at each charge that comes at you.
A brush takes 1 feather, 1 copper ingot and 1 stick. Armadillos live in savannas and badlands. Use the brush on one.
A target block takes 1 hay bale and 4 redstone. You must stand at least 30 blocks away and hit the very middle. Aim a bit above it, since arrows drop as they fly.
A fully drawn bow shoots the flattest. Shoot many arrows, and change your aim a little after each one.
Mark your spot 35 blocks away. Arrows that are stuck in the block show where you hit. They vanish after a minute, so keep shooting.
Brush up 4 pottery sherds. They can be the same or all different.
At a crafting table, put them in a diamond shape: top, left, right and bottom. Normal bricks don't count here!
A crafter takes 5 iron ingots, 2 redstone, 1 crafting table and 1 dropper. You need one of them first.
Put the same items into a second crafter, in the same slots, then power it with a button. Stand next to it when it crafts.
You have to fall from height 319 all the way to height -59 or lower, and live. Press F3 to see your height.
Dig a shaft 2 wide down to the bedrock and put water on the bottom. Water stops all fall damage, so this is what saves you.
Build scaffolding up the second column to the top of the world, and make a step right above the water. Step off and don't move: the fall takes about 8 seconds.
Creaking hearts are in big pale oak trees, in pale gardens. Mine one with a Silk Touch tool to keep it.
Stand two pale oak logs upright, one above the other, and put the heart between them. All three must point straight up and down.
Drink an ominous bottle (dropped by pillagers), walk into a village, then beat every wave. Prepare walls and iron golems first.
A honey block takes 4 honey bottles. You don't need a tall wall: one block with empty space around it is enough.
Place it 1 block above the ground and stand right next to it. Jump while touching its side, so you slide as you come down. It can take a few tries.
Any monster counts. Zombies are the easiest. Hit them with your best weapon at night, and stay near your shelter.
You need 41 monsters. The Bestiary tells you where to find each one, and shows which ones you still haven't defeated.
In this mod, some mobs only spawn at a higher Rank: skeletons 10, creepers 18, spiders and drowned 20, endermen 30, slimes 40, witches and pillagers 50.
Don't forget the strange ones: silverfish in strongholds, vexes from evokers, zoglins (take a hoglin to the Overworld), zombie horses, and the bosses.
Sculk catalysts are in the deep dark. They look dark, with a glowing top. The monster has to die very close to one.
Lure a monster right next to one and kill it there. Mine a catalyst with a Silk Touch tool to bring it home and use it safely.
Copper bulbs are in trial chambers. It must be lit, and it must have started to turn green.
Use an axe on it. If it's waxed, the first scrape only removes the wax. A shield in your other hand gets in the way, so sneak while you do it.
Put a lightning rod (3 copper ingots) on a pillar of stone at least 4 blocks tall, with open sky above. Nothing near it may burn.
Trap a villager about 6 blocks away. Closer and it could get hit and turn into a witch. Stay within 30 blocks of the rod yourself.
Storms are rare. Throwing a trident with Channeling at the rod during a storm makes the lightning come right away.
Trial chambers are deep underground, built from copper and tuff bricks. Explore caves below height 0.
Cartographer villagers sell a map to one when they've levelled up a bit. That's the easiest way.
A crossbow takes 3 sticks, 2 string, 1 iron ingot and 1 tripwire hook. Load it with an arrow, then fire it.
The mace takes a heavy core and a breeze rod. Heavy cores are rare rewards in ominous vaults in trial chambers.
A mace hits harder the further you fall, and hitting a mob saves you from fall damage. You need 47 blocks of fall, or only 14 with Density V.
Trap a mob in a pit and build a tower above it. An iron golem works well: it has exactly 100 health, so if it dies in one hit, you did it. Bring water in case you miss!
A jukebox takes 8 planks and 1 diamond. Meadows are grassy fields full of flowers, high up by the mountains.
You need a music disc. They're in some dungeon and mansion chests, or you get one when a skeleton shoots a creeper. Use it on the jukebox.
A chiseled bookshelf takes 6 planks and 3 wood slabs. A comparator takes 3 stone, 3 redstone torches and 1 nether quartz.
Stand between them with your back to the shelf and place the comparator on the floor, so its back touches the shelf. Books aren't needed.
You need an ominous trial key, and those need Bad Omen. Drink an ominous bottle, then walk into a trial chamber.
Ominous bottles drop from pillagers, or come from normal vaults. Then the spawners get stronger, and about 1 in 3 drops the key.
Use that key on an ominous vault: the dark one with blue light. Bring your best gear, since ominous trials are hard!
Suspicious sand and gravel look a bit speckled. Find them at desert temples, desert wells, ocean ruins and trail ruins.
Hold right-click with a brush on the block until it's done. Not every block gives a sherd, so try them all.
A bow takes 3 sticks and 3 string. Arrows take flint, a stick and a feather. Hit any mob, even a chicken.
Spiders only appear from Rank 20, so get string from cobwebs: break them with a sword. Or trade with a fletcher.
A bed takes 3 wool and 3 planks. Find sheep early, and sleep as soon as it gets dark.
It must be a normal skeleton, killed with an arrow from at least 50 blocks away. Skeletons appear from Rank 10. Strays, bogged and wither skeletons don't count.
Fence one in on open ground and give it a name tag, or put it in a boat, so it doesn't vanish. Hit it twice with an iron sword first so one arrow finishes it.
Aim high: at that range you shoot at about 45 degrees. A bow with Power IV or V can kill it in one shot.
A spear takes 2 sticks and 1 material (wood, stone, iron and so on). Hold right-click to charge it while you run.
All 5 must be hit in one run, and animals count. Fence a row of cows or sheep into a narrow corridor.
Mobs don't stand still, but armor stands do, and they count too! Put 5 in a row and sprint through them.
Do it during the dragon fight, or respawn the dragon. Hold right-click and keep it in the middle of the view for a moment.
Ghasts float over the lava in the Nether. Bring your spyglass, hold right-click and keep the ghast in the middle of the view.
A spyglass takes 2 copper ingots and 1 amethyst shard (from geodes deep underground). Parrots live in jungles. Hold right-click and look at one.
Make a T from 4 iron blocks, then put a carved pumpkin on top. Use shears on a pumpkin to carve it. Place the pumpkin last!
Stay within 5 blocks of it when you place the pumpkin, or it doesn't count. The space around the T must be free of other blocks.
Drowned sometimes drop tridents, and they appear from Rank 20. Look for one holding a trident, in rivers and oceans.
Hold right-click, let go, and hit any mob. Don't worry if it stays in the ground, you can pick it up again.
Evokers drop totems. They live in woodland mansions and come in raids. Cartographer villagers can sell a mansion map.
Hold the totem in your hand or off-hand, then get into a tough fight. It saves you the moment you would die.
Find a village. Villagers with a uniform have jobs. Right-click one to see what they trade.
Farmers are easiest: they give an emerald for some wheat, carrots or potatoes. Then take the item they offer.
Only YOU need to stand at height 319 or higher, and the villager just has to be close enough to reach. Press F3 to see your height.
Bring emeralds and something to trade. A villager without a job needs a job block: a stonecutter or cartography table is cheap and lets you buy emeralds right away.
Getting it up: start on the tallest mountain and send it up a water column over soul sand. Or put it in a boat, tie a lead to the boat, build up to 320 and jump so the boat swings up.
The 8 rare templates come from special places. This page shows which ones you're missing.
Spire: End city. Snout: bastion. Rib: fortress. Ward and Silence: ancient city. Vex: woodland mansion.
Tide: only from elder guardians. Wayfinder: brush suspicious gravel in trail ruins. Keep one of each!
Trim templates are in structure chests: pyramids, shipwrecks, fortresses, bastions and more.
At a smithing table: template + armor + a material like iron, gold or an emerald. Copy a template with 7 diamonds so you don't run out.
You need a crossbow with Piercing III or better. Phantoms come if you skip sleep for 3 nights.
Phantoms have 20 health, and one arrow won't kill a healthy one. Hit each one twice with a stone axe first, so it's nearly dead.
Catch two in boats placed in a line: a phantom that swoops into a boat stays stuck. Put an animal in the front seat so you don't hit the boat. Then line up and shoot.
Trial keys drop from about half of the trial spawners you beat, and there are some in chests and pots in the chamber.
A vault looks like a small black and orange cage. Use the key on it. Everyone in your group gets their own loot!
A lodestone takes 8 chiseled stone bricks and 1 iron ingot. Place it, then use a compass on it.
You need a trident with Channeling and a thunderstorm. Storms are rare and short, so be ready. It's a rare enchant: fish up or trade for a book.
Throw it at a villager with open sky above it, not standing in water. Lightning strikes it and it turns into a witch!
A raid captain carries a big white banner with a strange face. Kill it. Pillagers appear from Rank 50.
Wear leather boots, nothing else works! They take 4 leather.
Powder snow is on snowy mountain slopes. It looks like normal snow, but you sink in it without the boots. A cauldron out in the snow also fills up with it, slowly.
Wind charges come from breeze rods (1 rod gives 4). Breezes are in trial chambers.
Throwing one straight down isn't enough by itself. Jump at the same moment as you throw, and you'll go about 12 blocks up.
The kill must come from a crossbow arrow. Pillagers only spawn from Rank 50, so this one comes later.
Pillager outposts and raids are full of them. Keep your distance and use the crossbow until they're down.
You need the dragon alive! Hold a glass bottle and right-click in the purple cloud it leaves behind.
The cloud hurts, so have a bottle ready and be quick. Respawn the dragon if you've already beaten it.
There is only ONE egg in each world, on top of the middle portal. Be careful: if it falls and vanishes, it's gone for good. Hitting it makes it teleport.
Cover the portal first. Put a torch on the ground below the egg's block, then break the block it sits on. It falls on the torch and pops out as an item. Get it before you respawn the dragon.
Elytra hang in a floating ship next to some End cities. Not every city has a ship, so try several.
Take it from the item frame at the back of the ship. Watch out for shulkers, and bring a way down in case you fall.
After you beat the dragon, a small floating gate appears near the edge of the main island. Its opening is only one block high, so you can't walk in.
Throw an ender pearl right through the middle of it. You land on an outer island, so bring blocks and a pickaxe.
Go through the end gateway, then explore the far islands. Cities are tall towers of pale purple blocks.
Bring many blocks or ender pearls to cross the gaps. You just have to step inside the city.
First destroy the crystals on top of the towers with arrows. They heal the dragon. Some have cages: climb up to break them.
When the dragon lands on the middle portal, run in and hit it with your best sword. Stay out of the purple cloud!
Bring lots of arrows, blocks, food and Slow Falling. It helps to go with a friend.
It only checks that you move 50 blocks while you have Levitation. Shulker hits alone are too slow, so you need a shortcut.
Get hit by a shulker, then quickly throw an ender pearl up at a tall tower above you. The jump counts! Going down counts as well: throw it at the ground from high up.
Don't fall! Bring a water bucket, Slow Falling or another pearl for the way down.
You need 4 End Crystals. Each takes 7 glass, 1 eye of ender and 1 ghast tear.
Put one crystal on each of the 4 sides of the middle portal, and stay nearby until the dragon appears.
Give an allay one cake and play a note block nearby so it notices. Then drop a second cake on the ground: the allay carries it to the note block.
Allays are in cages at pillager outposts and woodland mansions. Free one, give it an item, and throw more of that item nearby.
Axolotls live underwater in lush caves. Find a cave with moss and glow berries, then use a water bucket on one.
Yucky food counts too: rotten flesh, spider eyes and pufferfish. Have milk ready to feel better. This page shows what you still need.
Farmer villagers sell apples. Poisonous potatoes are rare, so harvest lots of potatoes. Feed a flower to a brown mooshroom, then use a bowl on it for suspicious stew.
Chorus fruit grows in the End, and glow berries in lush caves. Enchanted golden apples can't be crafted: save the first one you find in a dungeon, mineshaft or ruined portal chest.
26 animals in total, and this page shows which ones are left. Each likes its own food, and the game shows when you can feed it.
Tricky foods: armadillo spider eye, axolotl tropical fish bucket, frog slimeball, camel cactus, fox sweet berries, strider warped fungus, hoglin crimson fungus, turtle seagrass, nautilus any fish.
Horses and wolves must be tamed first, and pandas need bamboo nearby. Mules come from a horse and a donkey. Sniffers need torchflower seeds. Do it in small steps!
Feed two grown animals of the same kind: wheat for cows and sheep, carrots for pigs, seeds for chickens. Then wait for the hearts.
You need all 11 cat colors. Most live in villages, and this page shows which ones you're missing.
Hold raw cod or salmon and walk up very slowly, or they run. Black cats only live at swamp huts, or spawn in a village at full moon.
A village only has a few cats. Move your tamed ones away so new strays can spawn, or visit other villages. It needs at least 5 villagers and 5 beds.
Place the egg on the ground and wait: on moss it hatches much faster. Then feed the baby torchflower seeds.
A fishing rod takes 3 sticks and 2 string. Spiders only appear from Rank 20, so break cobwebs with a sword for string.
Cast into water and watch for bubbles. When the float dips, right-click fast to pull it in.
Frogs make froglights when they eat tiny magma cubes. The block's color depends on the frog.
Temperate gives ochre, warm gives pearlescent, cold gives verdant. You need all 3 in your inventory at once.
Put your frogs on leads and take them to the Nether. Build a portal in basalt deltas, where magma cubes are most common. Frogs only eat the tiniest cubes.
Bring an axolotl in a bucket to a lone drowned in water, and let it out so it attacks. Bring two axolotls in case one gets hurt.
Hit the same mob yourself and finish it fast. You get Regeneration only if the axolotl is alive and not playing dead, and that's what counts.
A lead takes 5 string. There are 3 kinds of frogs, and a tadpole's color depends on where it grows up. You only have to put a lead on each once.
Warm: desert, jungle, savanna, badlands, mangrove swamp or the Nether. Cold: snowy biomes and the deep dark. Temperate: everywhere else, like a swamp.
Carry tadpoles in buckets and let them grow in small ponds in those biomes. Feeding slimeballs speeds it up. Water freezes in the snow, so put a glass cage and a bright light around it.
Glow squid live in deep, dark water, far from the sun. Kill one for a glow ink sac, then use it on any sign.
Use a smithing table: Netherite Upgrade template + diamond hoe + netherite ingot.
It costs a full ingot, more than most tools are worth. That's the joke! Do it when you have spare netherite.
Brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins. Bring water breathing and a brush.
Dried ghasts are near fossils in soul sand valleys in the Nether, or trade gold with piglins.
You can also craft one from 8 ghast tears and 1 soul sand. Place it in water and take care of the little one!
Sniffers dig up torchflower seeds and pitcher pods on grass. Plant one on farmland.
Hoe a dirt block next to water to make farmland. Plant wheat seeds, which drop when you break grass.
Wolf armor takes 6 armadillo scutes. Put it on your wolf, then use shears on it.
The armor must be damaged first. Punch your own wolf once: the armor takes the hit, and the wolf is fine.
Use armadillo scutes on the wolf until the armor is fully repaired. A badly damaged one needs more than one.
Goats live on high snowy peaks. Use a plain boat, not one with a chest. Place it right next to the goat.
Pull or push the goat into the boat with a lead or some wheat. It works on land too. Then get in the same boat yourself.
Put a campfire directly under the beehive, up to 5 blocks below it. Smoke keeps the bees calm.
Wait until honey drips from the hive. Then use a glass bottle on it. A hay bale over the fire keeps you from burning.
It must be a natural bee nest, not a beehive you made, and it needs a Silk Touch tool. An axe is the fastest.
3 bees must be inside. Mine it at night when they're home, with a campfire below to keep them calm. Check the tooltip of the nest afterwards.
Find a fish in water, then use a water bucket on it. Rivers have salmon, and warm oceans have tropical fish.
Tadpoles hatch from frog eggs. Frogs live in swamps, and sometimes tadpoles swim there too. Use a water bucket on one.
Feed two frogs slimeballs, and one lays eggs on the water. Slimes only appear from Rank 40, so a wandering trader or a swamp is your best bet.
Cats: feed raw fish. Parrots: feed seeds. Wolves: feed bones. Horses: climb on until hearts appear.
Skeletons (for bones) only appear from Rank 10. So a horse is the easiest first pet: no items needed at all.
Sulfur cubes live in sulfur caves, and in this mod they appear from Rank 40. They can swallow things.
Give a grown-up cube a block of TNT: throw it near, or use it directly. Then back away... fast.
Use an axe on a waxed copper block. One scrape is all it takes.
Use shears on a full bee nest to get honeycomb (keep the bees calm with a campfire). Then use it on a copper block. 9 ingots make a block.
Each wolf color lives in its own biome, and breeding won't give new colors. Bring half a stack of bones, and never hit a wolf: the whole pack attacks.
Pale: taiga. Woods: forest. Rusty: jungle. Spotted: savanna. Striped: badlands.
Snowy: grove. Ashen: snowy taiga. Black: old growth pine taiga. Chestnut: old growth spruce taiga.
That's every effect in the game, even from beacons, conduits, elder guardians and raids. Get a group of friends and a lot of planning.
Long effects like Hero of the Village go first. The short, nasty ones like Wither and Blindness go last.

You need 17 effects at once: Fire Resistance, Infested, Invisibility, Jump Boost, Night Vision, Oozing, Poison, Regeneration, Resistance, Slow Falling, Slowness, Speed, Strength, Water Breathing, Weakness, Weaving and Wind Charged.

Turtle Master gives both Slowness and Resistance. Add stone (Infested), slime block (Oozing), cobweb (Weaving) or breeze rod (Wind Charged) to an Awkward Potion. Slow Falling takes a phantom membrane.
Only the effect counts, not where it comes from, so stand at a beacon for some. Use long potions (redstone), and drink Turtle Master last since it's the shortest. Never touch milk!
A brewing stand takes 1 blaze rod and 3 cobblestone. It burns blaze powder as fuel, so keep a second rod.
Brew nether wart into a water bottle: that's a potion too, and it counts! Wart grows on soul sand in fortresses and bastions.
An anchor takes 6 crying obsidian and 3 glowstone. Use 4 glowstone blocks on it, one after the other.
Careful! Using an anchor with an empty hand outside the Nether makes it explode. Charging it is safe everywhere.
A beacon needs a nether star, and only the Wither drops one. Add 5 glass and 3 obsidian.
It has to work to count: put it on a 3 by 3 square of iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite blocks. That's 9 blocks.
A full pyramid has 4 layers: 9, 25, 49 and 81 blocks. That's 164 blocks in total, on a flat spot.
You can mix iron, gold, emerald, diamond and netherite blocks. Iron is the easiest: an iron farm with golems helps a lot.
Throw a gold ingot to a grown-up piglin (press Q), or use it on one while you hold it.
The trick: don't wear any gold armor! It only counts when the piglin would have attacked you.
There are 5: Nether Wastes, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Soul Sand Valley and Basalt Deltas. This page shows which ones are missing.
Basalt Deltas are the hardest to cross: bring lots of blocks and a good pair of boots. You only have to step in for a second.
Walking in the Nether counts 8 times! You only need to go about 875 blocks there.
Write down where your first portal is. Walk 875 blocks in the Nether, build a new portal there and step through it. Going diagonally counts too: 620 blocks each way is enough.
Bastions are big castles of black stone, full of piglins. You just have to walk inside one.
Wear one piece of gold armor so most piglins leave you alone. Piglin brutes with axes attack anyway!
Look for huge bridges and walls of dark red brick. Explore far from your portal, in one straight line.
Stand on high ground to see further. A pile of blocks and food helps, since lava seas block the way.
Only wither skeletons drop it, the tall dark ones in Nether fortresses. It's rare: only 1 in 40 kills, so don't give up!
A sword with Looting III makes it about twice as likely, 1 in 18. Kills by your tamed wolf count too.
Any chest in a bastion counts. Look on the bridges, in the hoglin stable and in the towers.
Opening a chest makes nearby piglins angry, even with gold armor on. Clear the room first, or grab the loot and run.
Each piece takes 1 netherite ingot, and an ingot takes 4 netherite scrap and 4 gold. Smelt ancient debris to get scrap. 16 debris in total.
You also need a Netherite Upgrade template per piece, and they're in bastion chests. Copy one with 7 diamonds and 1 netherrack.
Use a smithing table: template + diamond armor piece + netherite ingot. All 4 pieces must be in your inventory at the same time.
It's very rare and looks like dark, scratched stone. Look between height 8 and 22 in the Nether, most of all around 16. Press F3 to see your height.
Dig long tunnels at that height with a diamond pickaxe. Lava is everywhere, so bring Fire Resistance and blocks. Bastion chests can have a piece too, and that counts.
Experts blow up large areas with TNT, since debris survives explosions.
Blazes live in Nether fortresses, around a small cage on a platform. Only blazes drop rods.
Drink Fire Resistance if you have it, and hold up a shield against their fireballs. Snowballs hurt them a lot!
It's the obsidian with purple tears. Look at ruined portals in the Nether and the Overworld, and in bastion chests.
You need a diamond pickaxe to mine it. Or throw gold to piglins: they sometimes trade it to you.
Hit the fireball just before it reaches you. You don't need a perfect hit, and you can click as fast as you like.
The safest way: shoot the fireball with an arrow or a snowball. It flies the way you're looking, so aim at the ghast. One fireball kills it.
You need a saddle and a warped fungus on a stick. Saddles are in chests in villages, fortresses and bastions, or you can fish them up.
Put a warped fungus on a fishing rod to make the stick. Saddle a strider, get on it and right-click with the stick to steer.
Take a strider through a portal to the Overworld. Go through once yourself first, so the other side is loaded. A lead or a warped fungus guides it.
You have to get 50 blocks away from where you started, on lava. Going in circles doesn't count, and leaving the lava starts you over. Build a straight trench of lava.
Rain and water hurt striders, so ride underground or in a dry biome like a desert.
Make a T from 4 soul sand, then put 3 wither skulls on top. Place one of the skulls last.
Stay within 5 blocks when you place the last skull, or it doesn't count. Then run: it explodes when it wakes. Do this far from your home!
Any kill counts, as long as the ghast is in the Overworld when it dies. It doesn't have to die from a fireball.
Build a portal with its bottom edge at ground level, close to a ghast, so it can drift in without getting stuck. A fishing rod can pull it closer.
Trick: trap a ghast right next to the portal, go through to the Overworld, and shoot it back through the portal. Stay near the portal, so the area stays loaded.
You need a splash Potion of Weakness and a golden apple. Throw the potion at a zombie villager, then feed it the apple.
Weakness is an easy potion: no nether wart! Brew a fermented spider eye into a water bottle, then add gunpowder to make it splash. Spiders appear from Rank 20.
The cure takes a few minutes, and zombies burn in sunlight. Trap it in a hole with a roof and stay close until it turns back.
A shield takes 6 planks and 1 iron ingot. Hold right-click to block, and face the shot.
Skeletons only appear from Rank 10. No skeletons yet? A dispenser with arrows shoots at you too. Stand in front and power it with a button.
An enchanting table takes 1 book, 2 diamonds and 4 obsidian. You also need lapis lazuli, the blue ore.
Even a small enchant counts. Put in any tool with 1 lapis and pick the cheapest choice. You only need 1 level for that.
The portal is in a room with lava, deep in the stronghold. Its frame needs an Eye of Ender in every empty slot, up to 12.
The End is dangerous, and you land on an island far from home. Pack blocks, food and your best gear before you jump in.
A portal is a frame of obsidian, 4 wide and 5 tall, and you can leave out the corners. That's only 10 obsidian. Light it with flint and steel.
No diamond pickaxe? Build the frame in place! Make a mold from dirt, pour lava into it from a bucket, then pour water on it.
An Eye of Ender is ender pearl + blaze powder. Throw it outside and it flies towards the stronghold.
Walk the way it flies and throw another now and then. When it goes down instead of forward, you're above it: dig down.
Need pearls? Endermen come out at night from Rank 30, and they live in the Nether and the End too. Cleric villagers also sell pearls.
Pour water on still lava and it turns into obsidian. No need to find it anywhere else!
Only a diamond pickaxe can mine obsidian, and it takes a while. Chests at ruined portals sometimes have it too.
An iron pickaxe takes 3 iron ingots and 2 sticks. Mine a little more iron than you think you need.
A bucket takes 3 iron ingots in a V shape. Lava pools are on the surface and deep in caves.
Be careful! Put a block between you and the lava and scoop from the edge. Never dig straight down near it.
You need an iron pickaxe. Diamonds are deep: dig down to about height -59. Press F3 to see your height.
Dig a long tunnel at that height, and mine in stairs on the way down. Watch out for lava, and carry a water bucket.
Make a wooden pickaxe at a crafting table: 3 planks and 2 sticks. Then mine stone on a hillside or under the dirt.
Any one piece counts. Boots are the cheapest: only 4 iron ingots.
Any one piece counts. Boots are the cheapest: only 4 diamonds.
Iron ore is stone with tan spots. Look in cave walls and on hillsides. You need a stone pickaxe to mine it.
A furnace takes 8 cobblestone. Put the ore on top and coal or wood below.
A stone pickaxe takes 3 cobblestone and 2 sticks. It's made the same way as your wooden one.
achievement.progressive_adventure.tip.pr: Cod and salmon come often, pufferfish less. Tropical fish are the rarest, so keep at it.
They can bite anywhere, not only in warm water. Use a rod with Luck of the Sea and Lure, and take your time.
Treasure is a name tag, saddle, nautilus shell, enchanted book or enchanted item. Fish in big open water, away from land and bridges.
You need at least 5 by 5 blocks of water around the float, and a few blocks deep. The Luck of the Sea enchant helps a lot.
A diamond pickaxe takes 3 diamonds and 2 sticks. Dig down to about height -59 with an iron pickaxe to find them.
Follow a river to find new land, and take a boat over the sea. Cave biomes count too. Each ocean type counts separately.
Go far in each direction, and use waypoints to get back home. The Nether's 5 biomes count too, and so does the End.
Cold and warm oceans are separate biomes, and deep ones too. Boats make this easy!
A short walk does it. Press F3 to see your biome's name, and walk until it changes. Rivers and beaches count.
Villages are on plains, savannas, deserts, taigas and snowy plains. Stand on high ground and look for roofs.
Roads, farms and a bell show you're close. You only have to walk in.
You need 2 stones on, in different places. Right-click one, pick the other from the list, and stand still. It costs some XP.
Each new stone costs one shard more than the last: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. So 15 shards in total.
Only stones you turned on yourself count. Elites get more common at a higher Rank. Breaking a stone gives its shards back.
Waypoint Shards come from elites, the Tough monsters. The first elite you beat always drops one.
A Waypoint Stone takes 8 stone bricks and 1 compass. Place it and right-click with a shard in your inventory.
Start with what's close: cows, sheep, pigs and chickens. Rabbits like carrots and dandelions. Wolves and cats make a nice fifth, when tamed.
These count: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, melons, pumpkins, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, cocoa beans and nether wart. Torchflowers and pitcher plants too.
Grown ones only! Melons, pumpkins, cane, cactus and bamboo don't count if you placed them yourself. Let them grow, then cut the new part.
Wheat, carrots and potatoes are the easiest, and you can find them in village farms. Wait until they're fully grown.
Anything counts! Apples drop from oak leaves, and animals drop meat. Hold it and hold right-click to eat.
Cook every kind of meat and fish. Then try cookies, pumpkin pie, sweet berries and stews.
Yucky food counts too: rotten flesh and spider eyes. Have milk ready.
Trade with villagers for what you can't grow, and look further away: glow berries in lush caves, chorus fruit in the End, honey from bees.
Raw and cooked count as different foods. Eat a raw steak, then cook one!
Try everything from your farm: bread, carrots, potatoes, baked potatoes, beetroot, melon. Different animals count too.
Each Tough monster can have one trait: Swift, Frost, Blazing, Leaping or Summoner. You need to beat one of each.
The Bestiary lists traits on each mob's page, and shows the ones you've seen. Keep hunting at higher Ranks, where they're more common.
Three of them live in every ocean monument, in the big rooms. Near one, you get Mining Fatigue. Milk clears it, but it comes back.
Bring Water Breathing, Night Vision, or a conduit. Build a block shelter to hide from their laser.
Use a trident or arrows from a distance, and keep moving so the spikes don't hurt you. A kill must be yours to count.
Tough monsters are bigger and wear better gear. Look at one up close to see the word Tough in its name. They start appearing in the Overworld from Rank 5.
They get more common at a higher Rank. Bring your best sword and armor, since they hit harder.
Endermen wander in the End. Shulkers hide on End city walls and look like purple boxes.
Endermites sometimes appear when you throw ender pearls. Throw a few, and be ready to hit.
Keep defeating the same kind of mob. The Bestiary page shows how many more you need.
Pick something plentiful, like zombies. You have to do the kills yourself, so automatic farms don't count.
Explore new biomes and go down into caves. The Bestiary says where each mob lives.
Visit the Nether and the oceans. They have lots of mob types that you can't meet at home. The Bestiary shows which ones you haven't met.
Animals count too! Mix cows, chickens or pigs with the zombies you meet at night. The Bestiary shows what you've defeated.
Zombified piglins and ghasts are everywhere. Magma cubes like basalt deltas. Hoglins and piglins live in crimson forests.
Blazes and wither skeletons are in fortresses. That's usually the last stop.
Zombies come at once, but skeletons need Rank 10, creepers Rank 18 and spiders Rank 20. Keep playing, and they'll come.
Drowned come from Rank 20. Zombie nautiluses are in oceans, with a drowned riding them.
Guardians are at ocean monuments. Bring Water Breathing or a turtle helmet, and aim from far with a bow or trident.
Pillagers and witches appear from Rank 50. Vindicators and evokers are in woodland mansions.
Ravagers only come in raids. Drink an ominous bottle (pillagers drop them) and walk into a village, ready to fight.
Summon it underground or in a walled room, far from home. It blows up blocks and flies away from you if it has open sky.
At half health it gets a shield: arrows stop working, so use a sword with Smite. Milk clears the Withering effect.
Bring a few friends, Strength and Regeneration potions, and golden apples.
Stay alive from nightfall to morning, in the Overworld. Dig into a hill, close the hole with blocks, and wait. A bed makes it even quicker.
A full set takes 24 iron ingots: helmet 5, chestplate 8, leggings 7, boots 4. All four must be in your inventory at once.

bestiary.progressive_adventure.tip.minec: Burns in sunlight. Smite makes your sword stronger against it.
Burns in sunlight. Block its arrows with a shield or hide behind a wall.
Climbs walls. In daylight it leaves you alone unless you hit it.
Its bite poisons you. Drinking milk takes the poison away.
Hit it, then step back! Creepers are scared of cats.
Don't look it in the eyes! It hates water and can't fit under a 2-block roof.
Some throw tridents. They love to stomp on turtle eggs.
Doesn't burn in sunlight. Its hit makes you hungry.
Its arrows make you weak, so your hits do less damage.
Its arrows slow you down. Burns in sunlight.
Its arrows poison you. Shear it to get its mushrooms.
Cure it! Throw a splash potion of Weakness, then feed it a golden apple.
Throws potions. Fight fast, and drink milk to remove bad effects.
Splits into smaller slimes. The tiniest ones can't hurt you.
Splits like a slime. Fire and lava don't hurt it.
Sleep in a bed to keep phantoms away. Burns in sunlight.
Shoots fireballs. Snowballs hurt it, and Fire Resistance helps a lot.
Hit its fireball back with your sword or an arrow!
Its hit gives you Wither. Sometimes it drops its skull.
Wear something gold and it stays friendly. Give it gold to trade.
Gold doesn't calm it down. It hits very hard: bring good armor.
Peaceful until you hit one. Then the whole group attacks!
Scared of warped fungus. Hitting it with fire gives cooked meat.
Attacks everything, even other mobs.
Its laser hits from far away. Hide behind blocks to break the beam.
Gives you Mining Fatigue. Bring milk and your best weapon.
Its bullets make you float! Blocks or slow falling keep you safe.
Small and quick. Endermen hate them.
Hitting one calls more out of the stone. Defeat them fast!
Shoots a crossbow. A shield blocks the bolts.
Hits very hard with its axe. Keep your shield up.
Calls vexes and biting fangs. It drops a Totem of Undying!
Flies through walls. Defeat the evoker and the vexes disappear.
Very strong. Hit it when it's dizzy after you block its charge.
Jumps around and shoots wind charges that push you back.
Can't be hurt. Break its creaking heart to defeat it.
Blind, but hears everything. Sneak past it, don't fight it!
The strongest boss. Fight it underground so it can't fly away.
Break the end crystals on top of the towers first.
Protects villages. Give it iron ingots to heal it.
Tame it with bones. Hit one and its pack attacks!
Angry when it has cubs nearby. Leave the little ones alone.
Spits at you when you hit it.
Stings when angry. A campfire under the nest keeps bees calm.
Swim next to it to swim faster.
Rams you, even off cliffs. Careful near edges!
Get close and lightning brings skeleton riders!
Milk it with a bucket. Milk removes potion effects.
Milk it with a bowl to get mushroom stew.
Shear it for wool, it grows back.
Throw eggs for a chance of baby chickens.
Ride it with a saddle and steer with a carrot on a stick.
Trade with emeralds. Don't hurt villagers!
Creepers and phantoms are scared of cats.
Creepers are scared of ocelots too.
Sleeps during the day. Foxes love sweet berries.
Helps you fight mobs underwater.
Zombies want to stomp on its eggs. Protect them!
Eats small slimes and magma cubes.
Give it an item and it brings you more of the same.
Sniffs out and digs up ancient seeds.
Ride it over lava with a saddle and a warped fungus on a stick.
Every panda has its own mood: lazy, playful, worried or even angry.
Brush it to get scutes for wolf armor.
Keep riding it until it trusts you, then add a saddle.
